findings.quote: > **Exam signal:** "survive the loss of one Availability Zone" points to one group across several zones, with at least one instance in each Availability Zone.
findings.evidence: The signal has no 'but not if' for the case that decides fault-tolerance questions: 'with no wait for new instances' means static stability, where enough capacity already runs in the remaining zones (for example 3 zones x 3 instances for a load of 6). The chapter's own question auto-scaling-q021 tests this, but the prose never teaches it. Fact ec2-auto-scaling-wa-static-stability-for-az-loss (verified) is linked only from the question. Add the guard and one sentence in this subsection.
findings.resolution: fix-17: the signal now adds 'With "no wait for new instances", run enough capacity in the other zones: [static stability is preferred for high availability]' (ec2-auto-scaling-wa-static-stability-for-az-loss). The zone table it replaces repeated the Why line.

findings.quote: For the console, EC2 termination protection is the control.
findings.evidence: Correct option d depends on EC2 termination protection as something separate from scale-in protection. The chapter never teaches the difference, and this sentence of the explanation has no fact link, although verified facts exist: ec2-auto-scaling-scale-in-protection-ec2-termination-protection-for-manual and ec2-termination-protection-default-off-not-asg. Link the fact in the explanation, and add one row or one trap to the termination subsection ('scale-in protection does not stop a person from terminating an instance in the console').
findings.resolution: fix-17: q008 explanation now ends 'For the console, you [enable Amazon EC2 termination protection]' (fact already in q008.facts); an explanation-only change that cannot move the key, so no new verification. The scale-in protection Exam trap in 2-deep.md now adds 'Against manual termination, [enable Amazon EC2 termination protection]'.

findings.quote: | Which policies? | ... | It creates [target tracking scaling policies only](../facts/aws-auto-scaling.md#aws-auto-scaling-faq-creates-target-tracking-only) |
findings.evidence: The quote is correct, but in a 'Which policies?' row it tells a skimmer that AWS Auto Scaling has no predictive scaling. Fact aws-auto-scaling-faq-plan-dynamic-or-predictive-alone: a scaling plan can use dynamic scaling, predictive scaling, or both. Fact aws-auto-scaling-faq-predictive-ec2-only-in-plans: in a plan, predictive scaling covers EC2 only. Write 'Target tracking, plus predictive scaling for EC2 groups' and keep the link.
findings.resolution: fix-17: cell now 'Target tracking, and predictive scaling that [only generates schedules for EC2 instances]'. See claims-17-001.

findings.quote: At the default minimum healthy percentage of 90 percent, it replaces 10 percent at a time.
findings.evidence: Instance maintenance policies (minimum and maximum healthy percentage; launch before terminating) arrived on 2023-11-15 (fact ec2-auto-scaling-change-instance-maintenance-policy-2023). They change how both a refresh and a health check replacement behave. The chapter has no Changed recently note and no sentence about them, but card auto-scaling-c012 says 'without an instance maintenance policy', a term she has not met. RULINGS hard rule 7 asks for a Changed recently note for a change after mid-2022. Facts ec2-auto-scaling-maintenance-policy-launch-before-terminating-option and ec2-auto-scaling-maintenance-policy-terminate-and-launch can support a short note.
findings.resolution: fix-17: the instance refresh subsection now introduces the **instance maintenance policy** (term added to data/terms.json): 'With no instance maintenance policy, the minimum healthy percentage is [90 percent] ... Since [November 15, 2023], that policy decides whether new instances are [launched before or after existing instances are terminated]' (ec2-auto-scaling-change-instance-maintenance-policy-2023). Card c012 now meets a taught term. No Changed recently entry was added: the feature is new (it changes no old default value the exam assumed), and the fast Changed recently section has a 120-word limit that its two entries already fill.

findings.quote: | "instances fail the load balancer health checks but are never replaced" | Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) health check type | ... | you inspect the instance: suspend the health checks |
findings.evidence: The 'but not if' describes a different requirement, not a flip of the same stem. Two guards actually flip the answer here: 'the group has no load balancer' leads to a custom check with SetInstanceHealth (the twin in auto-scaling-q023), and 'new instances are replaced while they still start' leads to the grace period (q024). The exam answer for inspecting or updating one instance is usually Standby, which the chapter does not teach (see reader-08).
findings.resolution: fix-17: But not if is now 'the group has no load balancer: a custom health check'. Standby is now taught in 2-deep.md (reader-08).

findings.quote: **FAQ 6.** Can one group mix On-Demand, Reserved and Spot Instances? ... Yes.
findings.evidence: A bare 'Yes' suggests that a group launches Reserved Instances as a purchase option. In fact a Reserved Instance is a billing discount that applies to matching On-Demand instances. The verbatim quote can stay; add one sentence so that she does not choose a 'configure the group to launch Reserved Instances' distractor.
findings.resolution: fix-17: answer now 'Yes. RIs are a discount: you [receive your RI pricing for On-Demand Instances].' (ec2-auto-scaling-faq-ri-discount-applies-to-on-demand); the AWS quote is unchanged.
